acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Bears family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Ancient Ursine, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Den-Territory Sovereign archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Old broad-skulled apex bear with silvered mantle, broken claws, landmark pigments in its fur, and immense grounded weight.
Signature mechanic: Three Den Marks: the Ancient rubs one shoulder against a landmark to empower the matching lower-form behavior until that mark is broken.
battlefieldDuty: Claim three den landmarks and alternate roar, upheaval, and maul phases while commanding lesser Bears around the active landmark.
constructionDimensions: Stone and packed soil reinforce shoulder humps, paw backs, claw roots, and old scars while broad areas of fur remain visible.
Ground compression, rolling pebbles, and detached slabs emphasize weight without turning the animal into a golem.
counterplay: Break the active mark or draw the pack to an unclaimed zone, then punish the Ancient's exposed rubbed shoulder. Affinity signal: A load-bearing mineral seam opens across the planted paw, inner wrist, or shoulder after the heavy action.
forbiddenTreatments: Mineral growth that conceals the hook claw or recovery joints
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged ursine body, plantigrade paws, compact tail, broad muzzle, dense coat, and weight-bearing shoulder hump.
Escalation uses coat condition, scars, claw specialization, posture, and environmental interaction rather than humanoid equipment.
Raised shoulders, planted hind legs, open chest, and exposed inner wrists preserve readable commitment and recovery windows.
telegraph: The marked shoulder sheds fur and pigment onto one landmark before the corresponding phase begins.
